Causative Get and Have in the Passive Pattern
You can use causative get and have in active and passive voices. Let's look at how to use the passive pattern.

When you use the causative get and have in a passive pattern, it has the meaning of “arrange for someone else to do something”. You use this structure when you want to express that you pay or ask someone to do something for you.

The structures are:

get + object + past participle
have + object + past participle

For example:

I'll get my jacket cleaned.
I'll have those reports completed for you.

When you use the passive, you come across less direct and therefore more polite.
In the kitchen, any electrical appliances you use have got to be turned off.
We will have you sent there once in a while.
I'll have a copy e-mailed to you.
You can use other verbs, not just modal verbs, to express necessity.

You can use the verb to be + passive to express that something needs to be done.

For example:

Life vests are to be worn on the boat.
Rules are to be followed at all time.
The law is to be respected when you drive.

When you use this structure, you sound very official. For this reason, it is a good structure to use in the workplace.
Only employees who have been properly trained are to be operating the printing press.
All fire alarms are to be treated as a real fire, even if they are really a drill.

images.text:
Boris: Now, let's talk about the Workplace Safety Program. We will have it revised next year. It deals with preventing injury and illness to employees. Because you work in an office environment, you might think that there is no danger. In general, that is true.
Adam: All of the offices are on this floor?

Boris: We have several offices on the 16th floor, but we also have some space on floors 15 and 17 as well. There are a few things you've got to keep in mind. You need to know where the emergency exits are located. Remember, in the case of a fire alarm, you mustn't take the elevators. You must walk down the stairs to exit the building. If you hear the alarm, it may be just a drill, but you had better treat it as a real fire. The kitchen is equipped with a fire extinguisher. The kitchen staff has electrical appliances turned off every night.
Kristi: Of course.

Boris: Now, the more dangerous part of our business is the factory where the printing presses are located. We will have you sent there once in a while. I would read the guidelines specific to that area in the safety procedures manual. I'll have a copy e-mailed to you. I just want to highlight a few things. Most printing machinery accidents occur when the presses are in use. To prevent an accident, we have all moving parts tested every week. These areas have protection guards, but you will need to be aware about the dangerous areas. Of course, you needn't attempt to operate the machines yourselves. Only employees who have been properly trained are to be operating the printing press.
